correctness.rationale: Every pair of nonadjacent vertices in each of the two explicit sixteen-vertex strongly regular graphs has exactly two common neighbors. The proven diameter-two quartet biconditional is exhaustive for ordinary visibility. A complete 65,536-mask hypergraph census and a completely separate 65,536-mask BFS shortest-path census yield identical entire polynomial vectors and optimum sizes. An explicit adjacency-preserving subgroup orbit check covers all 96 rook and 32 Shrikhande optimum sets, and all single-vertex replacement trials fail. Both source programs were executed with recorded output.

value.rationale: The Shrikhande and rook graphs are the canonical nonisomorphic, cospectral (16,6,2,2) pair. Ordinary mutual visibility is a natural geodesic-set invariant, and its complete polynomials differ already in the number of minimal forbidden quartets, with contrasting maxima 10 and 9 and exact single-orbit optimum families. The census supplies a motivated benchmark beyond known scalar rook extremality; finite completeness here is a substantive classification.
